title: Mobilisation within 24 hours of hip fracture surgery and prolonged hospital stay: a case-control study
abstract: Objective: to estimate the association between mobilisation within 24 hours of hip fracture surgery and a stay longer than 28 days. Design: case-control study of 80 cases and 160 controls treated on one trauma unit in 2022 to 2024, with exposure read from paper notes. Analysis: logistic regression adjusted for pre-surgical characteristics. Results and conclusions will be written after analysis.
introduction: Trials in selected patients show shorter stays with early mobilisation, while adjusted routine-care data do not; the difference turns on confounding and on patients with dementia or delirium.
methods: Cases and frequency-matched controls were sampled from the unit's hip fracture list. First mobilisation was read from physiotherapy entries by readers unaware of stay length. The adjustment set came from a directed acyclic graph drawn before reading.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present sampling, reader agreement, exposure by case status, adjusted and sensitivity estimates, and the weekend-delay and dementia subgroups.
discussion: The discussion will set the estimate against the conflicting trial and registry findings and state what it means for weekend physiotherapy cover.
limitations: Residual confounding; notes of variable quality; one unit; modest power.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not claim that weekend cover shortens stays.
summary: STROBE-structured draft with results left empty.
